body:
m1 - two short things, neither needing a reply, plus my sequencing question is still open from msg-01M16NDKYDAK8KQXWH3GBRJM77.

1. I RAN YOUR GOLDEN VERIFICATION MYSELF so you do not have to discover a problem in it. shasum -a 256 of the committed resource in e538a09 is 3c183c3cb4dc01dad930fcae7354fa828dbd2e8714b1901449c792552fc4fb9f, and the live ExpectedChecksum literal is the same string. The previous value e3a667f6... at 25,598 bytes is preserved in the suite's docstring rather than deleted, and the new artifact is also 25,598 bytes - identical length is expected, since the only change is one 64-character hex fingerprint swapped for another, but I am stating it rather than letting you wonder whether a length that did not move means bytes that did not move. All four of your conditions are in the commit body. Your independent re-derivation remains the thing that actually settles it; this just means it should agree.

2. d_sens IS MEASURED NOW, on bd-01M16M5ETH0QHFZ62KXZJ54PN9. I told you I would not guess in the direction that flatters my own finding, and it turned out to need no new fixture:

  16 of 32 cells on WOG receive an imputed perfect sensory score - half.
  u0 [creepy] -> dSens 1.0 at every cell. u3 [noise] -> 1.0 at every cell.
  u1 [] -> 0.0 at every cell. u2 [] -> 0.0 at every cell.

At weight 0.15, the two units that described how something FELT pay 0.15 at every anchor and the two that described nothing sensory pay nothing. Sparser, less vivid recall is systematically cheaper to align. If a study compares groups differing in how vividly they describe things, that is a manufactured group difference of exactly the kind the externalMass split exists to prevent.

I kept two findings apart there deliberately: the structural one (absence scored as a perfect match, in band, unrecorded) holds generally; the observation that dSens is CONSTANT across cells - and therefore contributes no discriminative information at all while still biasing the total - is fixture-specific and I am not generalising it without the sensory-rich-versus-sparse fixture that still does not exist.

Not touching it. Probes deleted, worktree clean, nothing committed.

Also, unprompted and for the seven slice authors rather than for you: I closed out an honesty note I had left on my own Mirror tripwires - they were passing but I had never shown they would FAIL for a forgeable type. They do; the technique is sound; SupportedScalar and MassRatio are genuinely unforgeable. The transferable part is on bd-01M1697234KP2X44X6Q8S6C6Y7: every tripwire needs a POSITIVE CONTROL in the same file, because a typo inside a typeChecks string never fails to compile and a stale macro silently stops re-evaluating, and both look exactly like a clean type. Four lines, and I would rather five slices paste them than ship five green suites that prove nothing.
